newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slips on futures but premiums steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slips on futures but premiums steady.

text.p: NWE gas oil fell sharply on Thursday on heavy profit-taking in the IPE market, but premiums for physical oil were holding steady, traders said.
Nov gas oil, the new front month, cascaded $13.75 to close at $224.50 in a massive wave of profit-taking following a two-week bull run. "It's a mess in the market," said one trader.

The fall was accelerated by some traders' bearish interpretation of a report that German tertiary heating oil stocks stood at 65 percent of capacity at the end of September. They said the market was expecting an even lower number.
But most premiums held up despite the huge price fall.
Diesel cargoes were strongly bid following Wednesday's cargo trade at Nov IPE +$30 cif ARA and prompt supply was still short.
Also, German heating oil buyers continued to show interest for October barrels, after Wednesday's Nov IPE +$11 cif trade.

But heating oil barge premiums slipped with futures, trading down to Nov IPE +$7 fob ARA. One trader said the 170,800 delivery into the October IPE expiry would keep a lid on barge premiums. Most of the October longs were held by one company which shipped several cargoes over from the United States.
Despite the price fall, many traders said gas oil was still tight and expected a resumption of its bull run soon.
